rules.quote: Freya Bank calls customers who are 1 to 45 days late on one product. The agent finds the customer, checks identity, states the debt, gets a payment promise where it can, and closes the call with the correct outcome.
rules.applies: every call
rules.note: Order of the call: find customer -> identity -> debt -> promise -> close.

rules.quote: Every call starts with these. Nothing else is known before the tools are called.
rules.applies: every call
rules.note: No account fact (product, amount, days late) is known or may be said before get_account returned it.

rules.quote: | `customer_id` | `c_4f2a...` | Pass it to every tool call. |
rules.applies: every tool call

rules.quote: | `first_name`, `last_name` | `Daniel`, `Reyes` | The person to ask for. |
rules.applies: opening

rules.quote: | `title` | `Mr` or `Ms` | Address the customer as title plus last name. |
rules.applies: every call

rules.quote: | `now` | `2026-10-14T11:00` | The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock. |
rules.applies: every date or time calculation
rules.note: Example value 2026-10-14T11:00; 'today' always means the date part of now.

rules.quote: First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded.
rules.applies: first sentence of every call

rules.quote: Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified. This applies to everyone, including relatives.
rules.applies: before identity is verified
rules.note: Forbidden words before verification: collections, debt, payment, the product name. Also holds toward third parties.

rules.quote: Ask "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?".
rules.applies: right after the opening sentence

rules.quote: Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation. "Hello", "go ahead" and "who is this" do not.
rules.applies: while establishing who is on the line

rules.quote: Ask once more. If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `not_reached` / `unclear`.
rules.applies: the answer to 'Am I speaking with' is not a confirmation and not a third party
rules.note: At most 2 asks in total. Then close_call outcome=not_reached reason=unclear.

rules.quote: Answer a question from the customer first (rules 4 and 43). The ask that follows is the second ask.
rules.applies: customer asks a question (robot, scam) instead of confirming
rules.note: The question is answered, then the re-ask counts as ask number 2.

rules.quote: If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.
rules.applies: any moment of the call the customer asks robot/AI

rules.quote: Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of rule 1.
rules.applies: someone other than the customer answers

rules.quote: Ask when the customer can be reached.
rules.applies: someone other than the customer answers

rules.quote: A callback is for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 19:00, both included, and later than `now`.
rules.applies: choosing a callback slot
rules.note: Date in {today, next business day}; 10:00 <= time <= 19:00; datetime > now. Today must itself be acceptable only if a time later than now is left.

rules.quote: Call `schedule_callback` with the date and the time, then close as `not_reached` / `callback`.
rules.applies: third party gave a time inside the callback window
rules.note: schedule_callback(date YYYY-MM-DD, time HH:MM) then close_call outcome=not_reached reason=callback.

rules.quote: If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not schedule. Close as `not_reached` / `no_callback`.
rules.applies: third party offers a callback slot outside the window
rules.note: One re-ask only. No schedule_callback. close_call outcome=not_reached reason=no_callback.

rules.quote: If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close as `not_reached` / `wrong_number`.
rules.applies: the person says wrong number

rules.quote: If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.
rules.applies: the person says the customer has died
rules.wording: I am sorry for your loss.

rules.quote: A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.
rules.applies: someone other than the customer answers
rules.note: No verify_identity for a third party, no account information, no promise from them.

rules.quote: Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Call `verify_identity` with the answer.
rules.applies: the customer confirmed who they are
rules.note: verify_identity field=date_of_birth first, then field=phone_last4 (four digits). One question per turn.

rules.quote: Send a date of birth as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way the customer said it. The service rejects anything it cannot read as a date.
rules.applies: calling verify_identity with field date_of_birth
rules.note: API: an unreadable value returns ok=false and is not counted as a wrong answer.

rules.quote: Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.
rules.applies: customer gives the date of birth in digits only

rules.quote: A wrong answer may be asked again. Three wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.
rules.applies: identity check
rules.note: Counter is shared across both questions; the API returns wrong_answers_left, verified and all_verified.

rules.quote: If the customer gives day and month the other way round, `verify_identity` returns `hint: "day_month_swapped"`. Ask them to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as a wrong answer.
rules.applies: verify_identity returned hint day_month_swapped

rules.quote: After three wrong answers, do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch. Close as `not_verified` / `failed`.
rules.applies: three wrong answers in total
rules.note: No get_account, no amount even if the customer asks how much they owe. close_call outcome=not_verified reason=failed.

rules.quote: If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close as `not_verified` / `declined`.
rules.applies: customer declines a security question
rules.note: One explanation, then close_call outcome=not_verified reason=declined.

rules.quote: Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining. A second refusal or a second such question closes the call.
rules.applies: customer asks what the call is about instead of answering a security question

rules.quote: After both questions pass, call `get_account`.
rules.applies: after both security questions passed
rules.note: API: get_account is refused until both questions are passed. Returns products with product_id, type (credit_card | personal_loan | car_loan), card_last4, past_due, days_late, minimum_payment (cards), instalment_amount (loans).

rules.quote: Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment. Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan". State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.
rules.applies: right after get_account
rules.note: credit_card -> 'credit card ending <card_last4>' (4821 is an example), personal_loan -> 'personal loan', car_loan -> 'car loan'. Must say: collections team, late payment, product, past_due, days_late.

rules.quote: Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.
rules.applies: every date calculation

rules.quote: The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.
rules.applies: after both security questions passed

rules.quote: | 1 to 7 | early | the 12th business day after today | 1 |
rules.applies: product with days_late 1 to 7
rules.note: Band early: deadline = 12th business day after today (today not counted); 1 persuasion attempt.

rules.quote: | 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2 |
rules.applies: product with days_late 8 to 45
rules.note: Band late: deadline = 7th business day after today (today not counted); 2 persuasion attempts.

rules.quote: A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
rules.applies: every promise date

rules.quote: If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day. If the named day is after the deadline, rule 23 applies.
rules.applies: customer names a weekend day or holiday
rules.note: Next business day after the named day; if that would pass the deadline, offer the deadline (A19.valid).

rules.quote: If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.
rules.applies: customer gives a period instead of a day
rules.note: A vague period is not a refusal (A29.notrefusal).

rules.quote: "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week. So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.
rules.applies: resolving a weekday the customer names

rules.quote: If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
rules.applies: customer asks for a date after the deadline

rules.quote: Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". The agent proposes every amount.
rules.applies: asking for a payment
rules.note: First ask is always for the full past_due.

rules.quote: The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.
rules.applies: after both security questions passed

rules.quote: If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue. If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
rules.applies: customer says the full amount is too much

rules.quote: Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
rules.applies: late band, attempt 2 after the floor was already offered

rules.quote: If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it.
rules.applies: customer proposes an amount
rules.note: floor <= amount <= past_due.

rules.quote: Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
rules.applies: customer proposes an amount below the floor

rules.quote: First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
rules.applies: after stating the debt
rules.wording: Can you make this payment today?

rules.quote: A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with sections 7 and 8.
rules.applies: customer proposes a date or an amount
rules.note: Uses no persuasion attempt.

rules.quote: A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
rules.applies: customer refuses flatly or does not answer

rules.quote: Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
rules.applies: first flat refusal on a product

rules.quote: Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.
rules.applies: second flat refusal on a late-band product

rules.quote: When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Close as `no_promise` / `refused`.
rules.applies: a flat refusal with no attempt left
rules.note: Early: after attempt 1 is refused. Late: after attempt 2 is refused.

rules.quote: If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team.
rules.applies: customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss

rules.quote: If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`.
rules.applies: hardship customer accepts the support team

rules.quote: If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`.
rules.applies: hardship customer declines the support team

rules.quote: This rule comes before rules 30 and 41. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.
rules.applies: hardship mentioned
rules.note: Hardship beats persuasion and restructuring: a hardship customer who asks for lower instalments or a discount gets the support offer, not the restructuring transfer.

rules.quote: Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.
rules.applies: every call

rules.quote: Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.
rules.applies: before create_promise

rules.quote: If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against sections 7 and 8 and read it back again.
rules.applies: customer changes date or amount at the read-back

rules.quote: One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call. If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.
rules.applies: after a promise is recorded

rules.quote: Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`. If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`.
rules.applies: calling create_promise
rules.note: At most 2 create_promise calls per product. A 500 or ok=false is a failure.

rules.quote: After a recorded promise, say this sentence: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise."
rules.applies: after create_promise returned ok true
rules.wording: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.

rules.quote: "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close as `paid`.
rules.applies: customer says this past-due amount is already paid

rules.quote: "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close as `no_promise` / `dispute`.
rules.applies: customer disputes the debt

rules.quote: A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute. Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
rules.applies: customer says the product was closed or paid off earlier

rules.quote: A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.
rules.applies: customer asks for a new payment plan or lower instalments

rules.quote: A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`.
rules.applies: customer asks for a human, before or after verification
rules.note: Queue is general, close reason is human.

rules.quote: "Is this a scam?": say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, and continue.
rules.applies: customer asks whether the call is a scam
rules.note: No phone number is given in the brief: do not invent one (A44.unknown).

rules.quote: A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information. Do not invent figures, dates or reasons.
rules.applies: every call

rules.quote: If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `no_promise` / `refused`. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed as `not_verified` / `declined`. Rule 42 applies before and after verification.
rules.applies: customer says they do not want to talk

rules.quote: Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason. It is the last tool call.
rules.applies: every call
rules.note: API: nothing is accepted after close_call; reason required for every outcome except promise and paid.

rules.quote: | `promise` | none | at least one promise was recorded |
rules.applies: closing

rules.quote: | `paid` | none | rule 39 |
rules.applies: closing

rules.quote: | `transferred` | `restructuring`, `human`, `support` | rules 41, 42, 32 |
rules.applies: closing
rules.note: transfer_to_agent queue -> close reason: restructuring -> restructuring, general -> human, support -> support.

rules.quote: | `no_promise` | `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `service_error` | rules 31 and 45, 32, 40, 37 |
rules.applies: closing

rules.quote: | `not_verified` | `failed`, `declined` | rules 14, 15 |
rules.applies: closing

rules.quote: | `not_reached` | `callback`, `no_callback`, `wrong_number`, `deceased`, `unclear` | rules 6, 7, 8, 9, 3 |
rules.applies: closing

rules.quote: If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as `transferred` with that transfer's reason.
rules.applies: a transfer happens after a promise was recorded

rules.quote: Brief A never uses `add_note`.
rules.applies: customer with exactly one late product
rules.note: add_note is a Brief B tool. Reading built: get_account returning one product = a Brief A call, no add_note. See open_questions.

rules.quote: Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.
rules.applies: before close_call

rules.quote: Brief B is Brief A with a customer who can be late on up to three products. Every rule of Brief A applies unless a rule below replaces it.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

rules.quote: `get_account` returns one to three products. Each has its own `past_due`, `days_late` and floor.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

rules.quote: State every late product, one sentence each, before asking for anything.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

rules.quote: The band and the deadline are per product, from that product's `days_late`. Two products of the same customer can have different deadlines.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

rules.quote: First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today. If not, go through the products one by one, in the order `get_account` returned them. Do not ask about today again for each product. Start each product at attempt 1 of Brief A rule 30.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product
rules.note: Replaces A28.today for several products. After a no to all today, each product starts with the attempt 1 offer (last business day of this week, full amount).

rules.quote: Persuasion attempts are counted per product.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

rules.quote: If the customer names one date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back. The other products keep the date the customer named.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

rules.quote: Read all promises back together and ask for one confirmation. Then call `create_promise` once per product.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

rules.quote: The customer may promise some products and refuse others. For each product without a promise call `add_note` with that `product_id` and a reason: `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `paid` or `service_error`. This also applies when no product gets a promise.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product
rules.note: add_note(product_id, reason) before close_call, one per product without a promise.

rules.quote: A dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product does not end the call. Note it and continue with the others.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

rules.quote: A restructuring request still transfers the call (Brief A rule 41). Promises recorded before the request stay. Promises agreed but not yet recorded are not recorded. Close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

rules.quote: On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it.
rules.applies: any call that ends in a transfer

rules.quote: If one `create_promise` fails twice, keep the promises that were recorded and call `add_note` with reason `service_error` for the failed product.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

rules.quote: The outcome table of Brief A applies. With no promise recorded: if every product is noted `paid`, close as `paid`. Otherwise close as `no_promise` with the reason of the first product, in `get_account` order, whose note is not `paid`.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

rules.quote: With several products, `promise` wins whenever at least one promise was recorded, except rule 10 above.
rules.applies: get_account returned more than one product

open_questions: A46.nonote vs B8.notes: Brief A 'never uses add_note', Brief B says get_account returns one to three products and every product without a promise gets a note. For a customer with exactly ONE product, is add_note called? Built reading: one product = Brief A = no add_note; two or three products = Brief B = notes. Revisit if practice shows single-product calls expect notes.
A6.window: 'around eleven' and similar approximate times are booked on the stated hour (11:00). The brief gives no rounding rule.

A26.toomuch: the brief does not say which date the floor is offered on when the customer said 'too much' before any date was discussed. Built reading: ask today first, then follow A30 (attempt 1 = floor on last business day of this week).
B8 + A32: hardship in a multi-product call that declines support: built reading is one hardship note per product without a promise, then no_promise / hardship (B12.table).
A43.scam: the brief names no customer service number; the agent must not invent one.
